subject: MAP & commercial milestones: residency surcharge and cross-region failover terms
messages:
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandro Cortez <alejandro.cortez@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@acme-enterprises.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + pricing triggers for residency / failover fees

Alejandro / Sophie —

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion attached is a refreshed MAP draft (v2) with explicit milestone-based commercial triggers that map to ramp/commit thresholds and the residency premium. High level summary:

- Evaluation phase (30 days): limited usage at hosted tier — no residency surcharge applied during eval.
- Milestone 1 (P0 acceptance): commit to 50k tokens/day sustained for 30d -> 10% committed discount kicks in.
- Milestone 2 (regional residency): if customer requires US-only data residency + multi-AZ failover, apply the residency premium (described in attached matrix).
- Milestone 3 (ramp to scale): at 200k tokens/day sustained -> additional 8% tier discount and dedicated capacity evaluation.

Key commercial point we flagged in the call is cross-region failover. Customers that require automatic cross-region failover (active-passive in eu/us) are charged a failover allowance fee — this covers reserved standby capacity and higher SLA. We proposed two options in the pricing matrix:

A) Residency + failover as a bundled premium (flat percentage surcharge on top of committed rates)
B) Residency as a baseline surcharge + separate per-region standby capacity add-on billed as flat monthly fee

Ask: please review the attached MAP and the residency-pricing-matrix and confirm which option (A or B) you prefer from a procurement perspective. If procurement needs a blended number, we can propose a capped surcharge during the first 6 months of production.

I copied Rafael and Monica from Commercial Ops to confirm how the commit thresholds affect billing and how we would mirror discounts in the invoice when a milestone is retroactively achieved. Laura in Legal is looped on the follow-up email for any contract implications.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm preferred residency/failover billing option by EOD Wed (12 Aug)
- We finalize MAP and share updated SOW (if needed) by Fri (14 Aug)
- Target signature and funds release week of 17 Aug if procurement signs off

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-08-10_MAP_draft_v2.pdf; residency-pricing-matrix.xlsx; redwood-sla-terms-2026.pdf
From: Alejandro Cortez <alejandro.cortez@acme-enterprises.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@acme-enterprises.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme-enterprises.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + pricing triggers for residency / failover fees

Hannah —

Appreciate the clear write-up. A few quick clarifying points from our side after reviewing the matrix:

- Procurement leans to option B (separate standby capacity fee) because it lets us amortize failover costs across business units.
- A capped surcharge for the first six months sounds reasonable; can you confirm the cap in dollar terms rather than percentage? Procurement requested a $/month upper bound.
- For Milestone 1, we want the committed discount to apply retroactively from the date the threshold is crossed (not from invoice date). Is that supported?

Also procurement will need a short note on how residency is enforced (VPC routing, key storage) for their security team. Sophie: can you confirm if you want Redwood to provide a brief technical annex or would a bullet summary suffice to attach to our purchase order?

If you can update the MAP with option B as the recommended path and a proposed capped dollar amount for the standby fee, we can circulate to Procurement and Legal.

Thanks —
Alejandro
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Enterprises
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandro Cortez <alejandro.cortez@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + pricing triggers for residency / failover fees

Alejandro — thanks, good direction. Short answers inline and next steps below.

- Option B is fine — we’ll separate residency surcharge from a standby capacity monthly fee.
- Suggested cap: $25,000/month standby fee for the first 6 months for the configuration you outlined (US primary + EU passive standby, up to 4 reserved vGPU-equivalents). We can scale that down if you reduce standby capacity. Rafael / Monica: please confirm feasibility from Dedicated capacity planning.
- Retroactive discount: yes — we support retrospective billing adjustments for committed discounts. We will apply the discount to the invoice covering the period when the threshold was crossed and include a line item credit for prior usage in that billing cycle. That is how we’ve handled other MAP customers.

Security annex: we’ll provide a one-page technical annex (VPC flows, KMS key residency, audit-log export) for procurement to attach. Laura: can you and Legal sign off on the annex language — I’ll circulate a draft by EOD.

Rafael / Monica — quick asks for you both:
1) Confirm $25k/month standby is reasonable for 4 vGPU-equivalents in reserved standby for the first 6 months (we may bill lower if Acme wants less headroom).
2) Confirm process and timeline to issue retroactive credits when Milestone thresholds are met.

If we can get the internal confirmations today I’ll update the MAP to Option B with the $25k cap and send an updated SOW for Acme procurement review.

Best,
Hannah

Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP draft + pricing triggers for residency / failover fees

Hannah / team —

Quick operational confirmations after checking capacity and billing flows:

1) Standby capacity: $25,000/mo is feasible for 4 vGPU-equivalents in the first 6 months. That assumes we treat the standby as reserved capacity billed monthly with a 6-month minimum. If Acme requests auto-scaling of standby we’d re-evaluate pricing.

2) Retroactive credits: Commercial Ops can issue credits on the next invoice cycle once usage reports confirm milestone attainment. We typically need 7–10 business days to verify usage, generate credit, and reflect on the next invoice. We’ll include a milestone reporting annex in the SOW.

3) Billing workflow: initial invoices will include the standby fee as a separate line item. If milestone discount applies mid-cycle we’ll issue a pro-rated credit for the period prior to the invoice generation.

I’ll update the residency-pricing-matrix to include the dollar cap and add a short note on how standby capacity is measured (vGPU-equivalents). Hannah — I can circulate the updated MAP + annex for review by EOD Fri (14 Aug).

Monica Patel
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
